variant_reviews.comparison: For each graph node j in[d], let psi_j be its binary rejection decision and count false rejections only where the TRUE node degree is strictly less than k_tau. Divide that count by max(1,sum_j psi_j), then integrate under the graphical-model data law. Degree equal to k_tau belongs to the alternative, and the hypothesis family is nodes, not individual edges; retain the graph’s node-set convention in the bipartite and undirected settings. If no node is rejected the numerator is zero and denominator one, so FDP=0 without any undefined division. The displayed numerator’s upper d and H0 notation mean summing over null nodes within[d]. No library ingredient proves StarTrek’s control at level q merely from this definition.

Use the joint law P of all training and test observations and the measurable test-index rejection set R(Z) subset{1,...,m}. The true-null set consists of TEST indices whose marginal P_i equals P0, not the calibration index set or a set determined by estimated density equality. FDP is card(R intersection H0)/max(1,card R), and FDR is its expectation over the full data law, including any dependence and the score-fitting data. Empty R gives exactly zero. Because the random ratio is bounded in[0,1], it is integrable once measurable; do not replace E of this ratio by a ratio of expected counts or a conditional-bootstrap expectation.

At each fixed theta in R^n, let phi_i(X) in{0,1} be the measurable rejection decision, count the decisions at coordinates satisfying theta_i=0, and divide by max(1,sum_i phi_i(X)). Integrate with respect to the data law at that fixed theta; this is a frequentist expectation, not an average over a prior on theta. The null set is parameter-dependent and differs from a graph-degree or distribution-equality null. Empty rejection gives zero and the ratio is bounded, so ordinary probability integration applies. A sequence of procedures may depend on n, but that convention does not change the finite-n definition or imply asymptotic control.
